hypothesis: Can trained factual-action auxiliary source models choose actual interventions with higher real MountainCar goal success than shuffled-action trained model and identical factual model with permuted action labels, without any retraining?

intervention.selector: At each real public step use 8x4 P35 history of observed position, past real action/reward, past observed delta. Predict signed acceleration with each action candidate 0/1/2 using original frozen GRU embedding + original P35 aux_predictor(head concat one-hot), scale output by 0.0035. Let v=last public observed delta; choose argmax of (v+predicted_acceleration*0.0035)^2. Exact ties toward action 2. Do NOT use hidden true velocity, force or physics oracle.
intervention.permuted_control: Use same factual checkpoint but auxiliary one-hot action labels flipped 0<->2 for candidate scoring while actual physical action remains correct.
intervention.trained_sham_control: Use P35 originally trained shuffled-action auxiliary checkpoint, same selector.
intervention.meaning: one-step energy-motivated intervention choice, NOT full MPC, planning/general intelligence or autonomy

probe.method: At each probe index 0..7, reset three real original source worlds to identical public reset seed, replay identical deterministic random prefix (Python Random(seed+1977), first index actions); execute each of the three physical actions once on separate reset/replay source instances; use public position changes only, no hidden-state copy or true velocity. Compare exact 3-action outcome-effect ranking with model's predicted ranking, action-consequence real SHA and source MSE. Probe and heldout never used for updates.
